_comment: Boxes read by hand off the photographs, for works tools/detect_crops.py will
not cut. Both of these are shot in their frames, and a frame carries the same
browns and golds as the painting inside it, so the detector cannot tell the
one from the other and leaves the work alone rather than risk cutting it.
Each box was read from the brightness of the outer lines of the 960px
derivative, where the gilt lip of the frame stands out as a bright band and
the painting begins on the line after it. Both readings were then checked
against the museum's own measurement of the work: the proportions of the box
agree with the stated height and width to within 1.5%, which they cannot do
by accident.
SK-C-2: 38 lines on every side of 960x446. 884x370 gives 2.389 against the
record's 547x232 cm, 2.358.
SK-C-211: 12 left, 16 right, 21 top, 22 bottom of 960x814. 932x771 gives
1.209 against the record's 101x83 cm, 1.217.
SK-A-347 is not framed but is shot on its stretcher, with the tacking edge
showing on all four sides and a photographic colour chart along the bottom —
which the detector will not reach, being far deeper than a fiftieth of the
side. Painting begins at line 42 from the top, 41 from the bottom, 16 from
the left and 20 from the right of 960x1244, each read where the shadowed
brown of the tacking edge gives way to the sky or the foreground. 924x1161
gives 0.796 against the record's 68x54 cm, 0.794.
SK-C-1844 is on loan and is photographed in a deep carved frame that takes
about a seventh off each side. The sight opening runs 137 to 823 across and
121 to 683 down of 960x808. 686x562 gives 1.221 against the record's 45.5x37
